name: Hyaluronic acid pills

lead: Hyaluronic acid pills are oral supplements of hyaluronic acid (hyaluronan), the same molecule found in the skin, joints and in dermal fillers. Taken as capsules, tablets or powders, they are used as an inside-out approach to skin hydration, elasticity and fine lines, and some people take them for joint comfort that supports training.

A 12-week placebo-controlled trial of 40 healthy adults aged 35 to 64 found improved wrinkle assessment, skin hydration and elasticity compared with placebo, and a 2025 meta-analysis of seven randomised trials reported significant gains in hydration, elasticity and wrinkle depth. Researchers describe the trials as small and varied and call for larger studies.

paras: People take the supplement daily as a capsule or powder, often alongside collagen peptides, vitamin C or other skin supplements, for weeks to months. Studies assess skin at around 8 to 12 weeks. It is usually continued as an ongoing routine, with topical HA serums and sun protection used alongside.

Oral HA has generally been well tolerated in the trials reviewed. It is sold as a dietary supplement rather than a drug in the US, and product content varies by manufacturer. People who are pregnant, breastfeeding or on medication are commonly advised on labels to check with a clinician.

web.title: Oral Hyaluronan Relieves Wrinkles and Improves Dry Skin

chain: Oral hyaluronic acid absorbed and distributed
Skin hydration and elasticity rise in trials
angle.text: Taken daily as a capsule or powder, oral HA aims to raise skin water content and elasticity so skin looks more hydrated and fine lines look softer. Some people also take it for joint comfort that lets them keep training.

lead: Hyaluronic acid pills are dietary supplements of hyaluronic acid (HA), a glycosaminoglycan found throughout connective tissue and in high concentrations in the skin and joint fluid [1]. People take them in the hope of hydrating skin from the inside, improving elasticity and softening wrinkles, and some take them for joint comfort.

HA is a major skin component involved in tissue repair, holds water, and supports keratinocyte proliferation and migration; skin cells make less HA and break it down faster after UVB exposure [1]. The supplement idea is that ingested HA or its fragments can raise skin hydration and support the dermis, a different route from injected HA fillers, whose effects last about 6 to 12 months [1].

Randomised trials have tested oral HA on skin, including a 2021 study of 120 mg a day for 12 weeks in 40 adults aged 35 to 64 that reported better wrinkle assessment, stratum corneum water content, transepidermal water loss and elasticity than placebo [2]. A 2025 meta-analysis of seven RCTs reported significant improvements in hydration, elasticity and wrinkle depth [3].

paras: HA is a non-sulfated glycosaminoglycan made of repeating glucuronic acid and N-acetylglucosamine units, found in connective, epithelial and neural tissue [1]. It varies greatly in size, and its native half-life is short [1]. Oral products use HA of different molecular weights, including low-molecular-weight forms such as the 35 kDa hyaluronan registered in a 2026 trial for aesthetic improvement [4].

The main appearance use is skin: hydration, elasticity and wrinkles. A registered Japanese trial in healthy volunteers examined oral HA on skin [5], and a registered trial of high-dose oral 35 kDa hyaluronan included facial fullness, redness and dullness among its outcomes [4]. Marketing and wellness media describe oral HA alongside collagen and other skin supplements.

HA is FDA-approved as an intra-articular injection for knee osteoarthritis, and a 2020 meta-analysis found benefit for high-molecular-weight injections [1]. Lifters on forums such as T Nation have discussed oral HA for shoulders and knees [6][7]. Joint comfort matters for appearance only through the chain of staying able to train.
Evidence reviews describe injected HA for osteoarthritis, while trials of the oral form for skin are newer, short and small [2][3]. Reviewers call for larger, more robust trials [3].

A randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in 40 healthy Asian adults aged 35 to 64 gave 120 mg of oral HA daily for 12 weeks and found significant improvement in wrinkle assessment, stratum corneum water content, transepidermal water loss and elasticity versus placebo; percent changes were significant at 8 and 12 weeks [2].

A 2025 meta-analysis of seven randomised controlled trials found significant standardised improvements in skin hydration, elasticity and wrinkle depth with oral HA, while firmness, wrinkle volume and transepidermal water loss showed non-significant trends; the authors cited small samples and heterogeneity [3].

Registered trials include a Japanese study of oral HA on skin in 36 healthy volunteers (NCT05803083) and a 30-person trial of high-dose oral 35 kDa hyaluronan for facial fullness and dull skin (NCT07583108) [5][4]. Network meta-analyses of knee osteoarthritis treatments concern injected HA rather than pills [8].
The skin trials above did not highlight adverse effects [2][3]. Oral HA is sold as a supplement, so product quality and molecular weight can differ between brands.
